limitations: No FlashQuest/native or cross-native speed ratio: distinct measurement boundaries.
Recorded runtime observations passed production contracts; independent worker/server-log audit remains a separate final gate.
Internal all-pages arm pays scoring/top-k; it is not an optimized dense competitor.
FlashQuest and vLLM use the pinned AWQ checkpoint with different realized kernels; llama.cpp uses Q4_K_M weights.
FlashQuest fixed full INT4 KV allocation is shared across sparse/all-pages; vLLM reserves a fixed GPU-budget pool; llama.cpp allocates requested rounded context.
vLLM allocated_kv_tokens is a backend-reported group-aware request-capacity estimate, not physical cache-byte capacity; worker cache_tensor_bytes is separate.
Native memory covers load/warmup/request; native prefill/decode memory is unmeasured. Zero-point phase windows have no measured peak.
Sampled device peaks include display/idle use; owned RSS may double-count shared pages. Torch allocation and device residency do not prove absence of OS fallback.
The 12 GB board cannot close the actual 4 GB capacity endpoint; OS fallback and actual-target capacity remain unmeasured.
Fixed synthetic retrieval hits only; frozen confirmation failed 4/9 endpoints. No new noninferiority, general quality, novelty or final scientific-comparability claim.
